# Executive Summary {.unnumbered}

This document contains a comprehensive, hands-on validation and independent risk assessment of **Compass**, Solara Digital Bank's internal feature store and serving pipeline. 

As the Model Risk function's second line of defense, this assessment identifies critical structural, algorithmic, and governance risks within the system prior to the proposed expansions:
1. Powering the new **instant credit-line top-up** feature with no human oversight.
2. Lightening the current **change-review process** for feature transformation code.

---

# Data Flow — Batch Path

* **Trigger**: Nightly cron / manual `uv run batch-pipeline`
* **Formula**: $\text{mean}(\text{amount})$ where $\text{event\_timestamp} \in [\text{as\_of} - 30\text{d}, \text{as\_of}]$

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["transactions.csv"] -->|read_csv| B["DataFrame<br/>all 32,929 rows"]
    B -->|"filter: last 30d<br/>from as_of"| C["Windowed DataFrame<br/>per customer"]
    C -->|"groupby customer_id<br/>.mean()"| D["Dict: customer_id to avg"]
    D -->|for each customer| E["OfflineStore\n.write_features()"]
    E -->|INSERT OR REPLACE| F[("offline_store.db\noffline_features\nPK: customer_id, as_of, feature_name")]

    style F fill:#10b981,color:#fff
```

**Key properties of the batch path:**

* **Exact**: Arithmetic mean calculated over a precise time window.
* **Reproducible**: Same input data always produces the identical feature value.
* **Point-in-time safe**: Keyed by `as_of`, preserving historical values for backtesting.
* ❌ **Expensive**: Requires scanning the full transaction table on every run.
* ❌ **Latency**: Nightly cadence means features can be up to 24 hours stale at inference.

---

# Data Flow — Streaming Path

* **Trigger**: Continuous event listener / `uv run streaming-pipeline`
* **Formula**: EWMA — $\alpha \times \text{amount} + (1 - \alpha) \times \text{prev\_avg}$ where $\alpha = 0.2$

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A["transactions.csv"] -->|sort by timestamp| B["Ordered Events<br/>with seq index"]
    B -->|"resume from<br/>last_processed_seq"| C["Pending Events<br/>start_seq onwards"]
    C -->|batches of 50| D{"customer_id<br/>in running_avg?"}
    D -->|Yes| E["EWMA Update<br/>0.2 x amount + 0.8 x prev"]
    D -->|No| F["Seed<br/>running_avg = amount"]
    E --> G["OnlineStore<br/>.upsert_feature()"]
    F --> G
    G -->|"UPDATE SET value, computed_at"| H[("online_store.db<br/>online_features<br/>PK: customer_id, feature_name")]
    G -->|UPDATE| I[("pipeline_state<br/>last_processed_seq")]

    style H fill:#ef4444,color:#fff
    style I fill:#fbbf24
```

**Key properties of the streaming path:**

* **Fast**: $O(1)$ computation per event, requiring zero window scans.
* **Incremental**: Resumes from last processed position using `pipeline_state`.
* ❌ **Approximate**: EWMA is an exponential smoother, not a true rolling 30-day window.
* ❌ **Order-sensitive**: The output is highly dependent on the arrival sequence of transactions.
* ❌ **Silent staleness**: Does not actively alert or reject queries if ingestion falls behind the `FRESHNESS_TTL` (6 hours).

# Database Schema (ER Diagram)

The structure of the persistent SQLite databases backing the feature store:

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
    OFFLINE_FEATURES {
        TEXT customer_id PK
        TEXT as_of PK
        TEXT feature_name PK
        REAL value
        TEXT computed_at
    }

    ONLINE_FEATURES {
        TEXT customer_id PK
        TEXT feature_name PK
        REAL value
        TEXT computed_at
    }

    PIPELINE_STATE {
        TEXT key PK
        TEXT value
    }

    OFFLINE_FEATURES ||--o{ ONLINE_FEATURES : "same customer_id - no FK"
    ONLINE_FEATURES ||--|| PIPELINE_STATE : "state: last_processed_seq"
```

## Schema & Storage Comparison

| Property | Offline Store | Online Store |
|---|---|---|
| **File** | `offline_store.db` | `online_store.db` |
| **Table** | `offline_features` | `online_features` |
| **Primary Key** | `(customer_id, as_of, feature_name)` | `(customer_id, feature_name)` |
| **History** | ✅ Retains all point-in-time snapshots | ❌ Overwrites with latest value |
| **Staleness detection** | N/A (point-in-time specific) | ❌ Storage-level only; no TTL enforcement |
| **Feature Formula** | Exact 30-day mean | EWMA ($\alpha = 0.2$) |

```{mermaid}
classDiagram

        +get_features(customer_id, as_of) dict
        +close()
    }

    class OnlineStore {
        +db_path: Path
        -_conn: sqlite3.Connection
        +__init__(db_path: Path)

        +get_features(customer_id) dict
        +get_all_features() dict
        +get_state(key) str
        +set_state(key, value)
        +close()
    }

    class BatchPipeline {
        +run_batch_pipeline(as_of, store) OfflineStore
        +compute_txn_amount_avg_30d(df, as_of) dict
        -_load_transactions() DataFrame
    }

    class StreamingPipeline {
        +run_streaming_pipeline(store, stop_after_seconds) int
        -_load_ordered_events() DataFrame
        -_load_running_averages(store) dict
        EWMA_ALPHA = 0.2
        _BATCH_SIZE = 50
    }

    class FeatureAPI {
        +get_offline_features(customer_id, as_of) dict
        +get_online_features(customer_id) dict
    }

    class CreditScore {
        +score(features) float
        +decide(features) dict
        DECISION_THRESHOLD = 0.5
        _TXN_AMOUNT_AVG_WEIGHT = -0.01
    }

    class Dashboard {
        +run_health_check() dict
        -_sample_customer_ids(limit) list
        -_time_call(fn, args) tuple
        SAMPLE_SIZE = 50
    }

    BatchPipeline --> OfflineStore : writes to
    StreamingPipeline --> OnlineStore : writes to
    FeatureAPI --> OfflineStore : reads from
    FeatureAPI --> OnlineStore : reads from
    CreditScore ..> FeatureAPI : consumes features
    Dashboard ..> FeatureAPI : probes health
```

# The Core Risk: Training/Serving Skew

Training/Serving skew is the most significant structural risk identified in Compass. It violates the core assumption of machine learning model stability: **that the serving-time feature distribution matches the training-time feature distribution.**

```{mermaid}
graph TB
    subgraph Training["Model Training - Underwriting"]
        T1["Training Data Source:<br/>Offline Store"]
        T2["Feature: txn_amount_avg_30d<br/>= EXACT arithmetic mean<br/>over rolling 30d window"]
        T3["Model learns weights<br/>against EXACT mean values"]
        T1 --> T2 --> T3
    end

    subgraph Serving["Model Serving - In-App Real-Time"]
        S1["Serving Data Source:<br/>Online Store"]
        S2["Feature: txn_amount_avg_30d<br/>= EWMA with alpha=0.2<br/>exponential smoother"]
        S3["Model receives EWMA values<br/>a DIFFERENT distribution!"]
        S1 --> S2 --> S3
    end

    subgraph Impact["Impact"]
        I1["Training/Serving Skew<br/>hidden covariate shift"]
        I2["Model scores are miscalibrated<br/>for real-time decisions"]
        I3["Automatic credit top-ups<br/>approved or denied incorrectly"]
    end

    T3 -->|"SKEW"| I1
    S3 -->|"SKEW"| I1
    I1 --> I2 --> I3

    style I1 fill:#ef4444,color:#fff
    style I2 fill:#f59e0b,color:#fff
    style I3 fill:#dc2626,color:#fff
```

## Quantifying the Skew (Empirical Validation)

Running the query CLI for customer `C0001` reveals a severe mathematical divergence:

$$\text{Offline (Batch): } 142.41 \quad\text{vs.}\quad \text{Online (Streaming): } 76.82 \quad (\Delta \approx 46\%)$$

### Mathematical Divergence: Exact Mean vs. EWMA

* **Exact Mean (Batch)** treats all transactions within the 30-day window with equal weight ($1/N$).
* **EWMA (Online)** discounts older transactions exponentially. Since $\alpha = 0.2$, the most recent transaction holds $20\%$ of the total weight, while transactions older than a few days contribute almost nothing.

This difference creates a **covariate shift** in the features. Downstream models trained on the exact mean will predict incorrectly when evaluated using EWMA inputs.

# Risk Mapping & Business Case Incidents

## Incident Analysis

| Incident (from Business Case) | Technical Root Cause | Code Location | Risk Category |
|---|---|---|---|
| Customer complaint: limit based on "outdated transaction pattern" | Ingestion lagging silently. `FRESHNESS_TTL = 6h` is defined in config, but **never validated** at read time. | `online_store.py`<br/>`config.py` | **Silent Staleness** |
| Real-time limit adjustments inconsistent with underwriting score | Discrepancy in feature definitions. Training uses exact mean; serving uses EWMA. | `batch_pipeline.py` L28 vs. `streaming_pipeline.py` L72 | **Training/Serving Skew** |
| Uptime is 100% on dashboard, but credit score quality has degraded | Monitoring is limited to API health (HTTP status, latency). No statistical or data freshness checks exist. | `monitoring/dashboard.py` | **Blind Monitoring** |

## Risk Assessment Heat Map

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Priority / Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Training/Serving Skew** | High (0.90) | Critical (0.95) | 🔴 **Critical** (Fix Immediately) |
| **No Human Review** | Medium-High (0.70) | Critical (0.90) | 🔴 **Critical** (Fix Immediately) |
| **Silent Staleness** | High (0.80) | High (0.85) | 🟠 **High** (Fix Before Launch) |
| **Blind Monitoring** | Very High (0.95) | Medium-High (0.70) | 🟡 **Medium** (Monitor & Alert) |

# Proposed Solution Architecture

To safely proceed with automated credit-line top-ups, Solara must implement a series of architectural safeguards:

```{mermaid}
graph TB
    subgraph FIX1["Fix 1: Unify Feature Logic"]
        F1A["Extract shared compute_txn_amount_avg_30d()"]
        F1B["Streaming approximates window\nwith a sliding buffer"]
        F1C["OR: document EWMA explicitly\nand train the online model on EWMA features"]
        F1A --> F1B
        F1A --> F1C
    end

    subgraph FIX2["Fix 2: Enforce Freshness TTL"]
        F2A["OnlineStore.get_features() checks computed_at"]
        F2B["If age > FRESHNESS_TTL then raise StaleFeatureError"]
        F2C["feature_api falls back to offline store\nor rejects the request"]
        F2A --> F2B --> F2C
    end

    subgraph FIX3["Fix 3: Monitoring with Drift Detection"]
        F3A["Add feature_drift_monitor()"]
        F3B["Compare online vs offline feature distributions"]
        F3C["Alert if mean delta > threshold (e.g. 15%)"]
        F3D["Track P50/P95 of feature staleness age"]
        F3A --> F3B --> F3C
        F3A --> F3D
    end

    subgraph FIX4["Fix 4: Human Review Gate"]
        F4A["Automated approval only if:<br/>feature_age < 1h<br/>online vs offline delta < 15%<br/>customer has > 30 days history"]
        F4B["Otherwise queue for human review"]
        F4A --> F4B
    end

    FIX1 --> FIX2 --> FIX3 --> FIX4
```

## Before vs. After Controls

| Control | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Feature Formula** | Divergent (Exact Mean vs. EWMA) | Unified (Same arithmetic logic) |
| **Freshness Validation** | ❌ None (Stale data served silently) | ✅ Read-time verification (Age vs. TTL) |
| **Monitoring Dashboard** | Latency & uptime only | Uptime, Latency, Staleness P95, Feature Drift |
| **Top-up Process** | Automatic approval with zero fallback | Automated gate with fallback to manual review |

# 2. Run both computation pipelines
